title: Rc Linux Artifact
objective: Build and validate a relocatable unsigned Linux x64 release candidate from a clean environment, including cold/warm startup and native capability loading.

handoff.summary: Added deterministic, installer-compatible Linux x64 release packaging and a clean-environment validator for both standalone executables. The validator extracts the archive, installs it through install.sh, removes Node and package-manager paths, uses fresh runtime state, exercises Python and exact native mathematics, checks generated FLINT/FFLAS/M4RI traces, records cold/warm timing and cache evidence, and proves byte-identical archive generation. On the validated glibc 2.43 host the archive is 159180380 bytes with SHA-256 c117aeb421224d611c5f8b2063473ebb9dc4d7350aabdcabd6ee945260245718.
risks: The candidate was built on glibc 2.43; public Linux artifacts must be rebuilt and tested on the project's oldest supported glibc baseline.

The portable tier was run and reached only the expected manifest ratchet failure because test/release-candidate-linux.cjs is not yet registered in the shared node-test manifest; that shared registration is deliberately outside this lane's claim.
Signing and publication are intentionally outside this unsigned Linux candidate lane.
next_steps: Register test/release-candidate-linux.cjs in test/node-test-manifest.cjs and rerun pnpm test:portable in integration.
Wire the validator into release CI after the embedded build-receipt work lands, then rebuild on the oldest supported Linux runtime.
Retain the generated archive and JSON report as release evidence, but do not commit either build artifact.
